capabilities: Keep task lines consistent between collections and daily logs
File tasks into collections and mark the original line
Build day logs ahead with meetings from .ics or CalDAV calendars
Create and link meeting notes for calendar meetings
Review unprocessed notes and track diary and review streaks
disambiguation: Despite the name, it does not automate decisions: moving a task to another day or collection is always something you choose, one task at a time.
extras: Task consistency does not run on phones; no promise it works alongside Day Planner; published .ics links are stored in the vault's settings file and treated as passwords; the manifest notes it has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff; the plugin stays on 0.x versions.
motivation: The author built it for their own way of working, growing out of Ryder Carroll's bullet journal method, and published it in case it suits others.
problem: Obsidian has no way to keep a task written in a collection and its copy in a day's log in sync, so people copy and update task lines between pages by hand.

relations.evidence: Effortless reads and writes the Tasks plugin's own task-line format
It grew out of Ryder Carroll's bullet journal method and takes what works from it

requires.name: calendar account (e.g. iCloud over CalDAV) for signed-in calendar sources

summary: Task and daily-log system in plain notes that keeps each task consistent between its collection and the day's log, inspired by the bullet journal method.
